title: Sebastian under water: what the flood warnings said, what is closed, and what to do at your house now
seoTitle: Sebastian Flooding: Closures and What to Do Now
description: Weather service warnings covering Sebastian said 16 to 22 inches of rain fell. Road closures, the polling place move, and what to do about septic and wells.
dek: Sebastian took some of the heaviest rain on the Treasure Coast this week. Roads in Sebastian Highlands closed, a polling place moved, and the county is under a state of emergency. Here is what Sebastian homeowners should do while the water drains.
facebook: Did your Sebastian street turn into a canal this week? You're not imagining how much rain fell. Here's what the weather service measured, which roads and places closed, and the septic and well mistakes to avoid while the ground is soaked.

body.text: Sebastian homeowners have been watching the rain gauge all week, and the numbers are hard to believe. On Monday afternoon, Nov. 2, the National Weather Service in Melbourne issued a flood warning for southeastern Brevard and northeastern Indian River counties, naming Sebastian, Sebastian Inlet and Wabasso. It said 16 to 22 inches of rain had fallen across that area, with another 1 to 2 inches possible.

That came on top of a soggy weekend. Sebastian Daily reported Monday morning that some areas had already picked up 3 to 7 inches, and that the ground was nearly saturated, raising the risk of flooding on roads and in poorly drained spots. Here is where things stand and what to do at your own house.

body.title: The short version
body.text: Indian River County is under a local state of emergency that took effect at 2:30 p.m. Monday and lasts until further order. The governor also declared a state of emergency for seven counties, including Indian River. Roads in Sebastian Highlands were closed Monday. Indian River County schools are closed Tuesday, Nov. 3. Precinct 7 voters now vote at the Sebastian Elks Lodge, 2714 South Fleming St. Do not pump a septic tank while the ground is soaked.
What is closed or changed in Sebastian

TCPalm reported Monday that roads within the Sebastian Highlands neighborhood were closed because of flooding. The county said numerous roads had become impassable and asked residents to avoid nonessential travel, to obey road closures and barricades, and not to drive through flooded roads.

All five Indian River County customer convenience centers, including the one in Roseland, were closed Monday because of overnight flooding. Indian River County schools are closed today, Tuesday, Nov. 3.

Today is also Election Day. Because of flooding at the Sebastian Church of God, 281 Delaware, the Supervisor of Elections moved Precinct 7 to the Sebastian Elks Lodge at 2714 South Fleming St., which is also the Precinct 8 polling place. Polls are open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Questions go to the Supervisor of Elections at 772-226-4700 or voteindianriver.gov.
Your septic tank: wait before you pump

If your Sebastian home is on septic, this is the week to be gentle with it. When the ground is this wet, the drainfield has nowhere to send water. The Florida Department of Health in St. Lucie County told residents not to have septic tanks pumped while groundwater is this high, and to conserve water if plumbing is slow.

The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency explains why. Pumping a tank in saturated soil is only a short-term fix, and an empty tank can rise out of the ground and damage its pipes. Keep cars and mowers off the drainfield while the soil is soft. Once the water goes down, the EPA says to have the tank checked if you see signs of damage, such as settling or a system that will not take water.
Your well: test before you trust it

If floodwater reached your wellhead, or you cannot tell, health officials say to use bottled or boiled water for drinking, ice, brushing teeth and cleaning cuts until the well is tested. Private well questions for Indian River County go to the Florida Department of Health in Indian River County, 1900 27th St., Vero Beach, phone 772-794-7440.

Mold starts fast in a Florida house. The CDC says to clean and dry wet items, or remove them, within 24 to 48 hours. Leave flooded electrical and mechanical equipment alone until it is dry and clean. Avoid touching floodwater, especially with an open cut, and wash any wound with soap.
Who to call at the City of Sebastian

For drainage problems on your street, use the city's online Report a Concern portal, linked from the front page of cityofsebastian.org. For flood questions and elevation certificates, the city lists Community Development at 772-589-5518. The Building Department is 772-589-5537. City Hall is at 1225 Main St. and is open 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, closed noon to 1 p.m. The city's Flooding and Hurricane Preparedness page links to flood maps and a real-time water level gauge, and you can sign up for city alerts through Notify Me.

items: Stay off flooded streets. If a road in the Highlands has water on it, treat it as closed.
On septic? Cut back on water use, hold off on laundry, and do not pump the tank until the ground dries.
On a well? If it may have flooded, drink bottled or boiled water and call 772-794-7440 about testing.
If water got inside, start drying within 24 to 48 hours.
Report blocked drainage or standing water problems through the city's Report a Concern portal.
Voting in Precinct 7? Go to the Elks Lodge at 2714 South Fleming St., not the church on Delaware.
Stay off the beach. A high rip current risk for coastal Indian River County runs through late Tuesday night.

body.text: Sebastian Daily, citing the weather service, reported that conditions should improve midweek, with more sunshine by Thursday. Give the swales and ditches a few dry days to catch up.
